title: Quota Exceeded
description: A partner's CSV import contains a large batch with a deliberate mix of valid rows, rows missing required columns, and rows with an unknown customer email — simulating a real-world messy export from a legacy system. Confirm the import handles a sizeable, heterogeneous batch correctly end to end.
successCondition: POST /api/admin/shipments/import as admin with a 10-data-row CSV: 6 fully valid rows referencing existing customer accounts, 2 rows missing one required column each, and 2 rows with a customerEmail that was never registered. The response is 200 with totalRows 10, accepted 6, rejected 4. Every rejected row's status is "rejected" with a non-empty errors array, and every accepted row's status is "accepted" with a shipmentId. GET /api/tracking as an admin (or per-customer) afterward confirms exactly 6 new shipments exist that weren't there before the import.
hints: row numbers in the response are 1-indexed counting the header as row 1, so your first data row is reported as row 2 — use that to match each result back to the row you wrote.
Register the customer accounts you intend to reference before building the CSV, and deliberately leave the other two emails unregistered.
